name: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of clinical features suggestive of systemic autoimmune disease but not fulfilling criteria for defined connective tissue diseases
Presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) or other autoantibodies without specific disease-defining serology
Exclusion of other defined connective tissue diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, or mixed connective tissue disease
Supportive laboratory abnormalities such as elevated ESR or CRP

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features suggestive of systemic autoimmune disease plus positive ANA and exclusion of other defined connective tissue diseases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and by exclusion; no standardized criteria exist

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) or C-reactive protein (CRP)
imaging: Chest X-ray may show mild pleural effusion or interstitial changes
other: Exclusion of other connective tissue diseases by clinical and serological criteria

distinguishingFeatures: Specific clinical criteria such as malar rash, renal involvement, and immunologic markers (anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm antibodies)
More defined organ involvement and disease-specific autoantibodies
Overlapping features of lupus, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis
Specific autoantibodies such as anti-centromere or anti-Scl-70

redFlags: Rapidly progressive organ involvement (renal, pulmonary, cardiac)
Severe constitutional symptoms such as high-grade fever or weight loss
references: American College of Rheumatology guidelines on undifferentiated connective tissue disease
